releases.body:
## What's Changed

### Longer custom review instructions

`reviewer.instructions` was capped at 4,000 characters. The new `reviewer.maxInstructionsChars` option raises that cap (4,000–200,000; the default stays 4,000).

```jsonc
"reviewer": {
  "instructions": ["…a longer review policy…"],
  "maxInstructionsChars": 20000
}
```

- Instructions are sent, and billed, with every review and count toward each reviewer's size limit: `maxInputBytes` for the `agent` and `chat` reviewers, and `maxStateTokens` (or `longContext.maxStateTokens`) for the `decision` backend. Instructions that would fill a limit in use now make the plugin fail at startup instead of escalating every review.
- The `decision` backend now counts the instructions in its size estimate and in its check that the model read the whole prompt.
- Near the top of the range, raise `maxInputBytes` as well; with `longContext`, instructions larger than `maxStateTokens` send every review with long context.

* feat: let users raise the reviewer.instructions length limit by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/62

### Security hardening

- Prompts of subagent (child) sessions are no longer treated as user intent: a review uses the root session's latest prompt and conversation, and a new prompt in the root session cancels a subagent's pending allow. A failed or slow root lookup fails closed.
- The Codex SDK reviewer now runs with `approvalPolicy: "never"` in its read-only sandbox, so its automatic reviewer can no longer approve running outside the sandbox (this replaces the auto mode chosen for Codex in v0.8.0; the Claude Agent SDK reviewer is unchanged).
- The publish workflow verifies the release source before installing anything and installs and publishes with `--ignore-scripts`.

* fix: harden subagent user intent, Codex approvals and the publish workflow by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/58

### Dependencies

* ci(deps): bump jdx/mise-action from 5.1.2 to 5.2.1 in the all-actions group by @dependabot in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/59
* chore(deps): bump the all-dependencies group with 93 updates by @dependabot in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/60

## Contributors

* @dyoshikawa

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/compare/v0.9.0...v0.10.0

## What's Changed

### Chat backend: OpenAI and Anthropic API keys

`reviewer.chat.provider` lets the `chat` backend call the OpenAI or Anthropic API directly with their own keys:

| `reviewer.chat.provider` | Endpoint | Key when `reviewer.chat.apiKey` is unset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"openai-compatible"` (default, unchanged) | `<baseURL>/chat/completions` | `AUTO_APPROVAL_CHAT_API_KEY` |
| `"openai"` | `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `"anthropic"` | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` (Messages API) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |

```jsonc
"reviewer": {
  "backend": "chat",
  "chat": { "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-haiku-5-5" }
}
```

- The vendor providers always call the vendor's own host and take no `baseURL`, so their key never reaches another server.
- The Anthropic provider uses the native Messages API (`x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `max_tokens: 16000`). Only a finished reply (`end_turn` / `stop_sequence`) is read for a verdict; a refusal or any other early stop fails the review, and "prompt is too long" or running out of context window counts as too large.
- Works for the decision backend's `onOversize: "chat"` fallback too.

* feat: call the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs from the chat backend by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/56

## Contributors

* @dyoshikawa

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/compare/v0.8.0...v0.9.0

## What's Changed

### Agent runtimes: Claude Agent SDK and Codex SDK

The `agent` reviewer can now run outside OpenCode. `reviewer.agent.runtime` picks where:

- `"opencode"` (default, unchanged): a read-only OpenCode session.
- `"claude-agent-sdk"`: Claude Code through `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, with only `Read`/`Glob`/`Grep`, `permissionMode: "auto"`, and no settings, hooks, MCP servers or plugins loaded from disk.
- `"codex-sdk"`: Codex through `@openai/codex-sdk`, in the read-only sandbox without network or web search, in auto mode (`approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"`), and without the project's `AGENTS.md`.

Both SDKs are optional peer dependencies. OpenCode does not install them with the plugin, so install the one you use globally and point `reviewer.agent.claudeAgentSdk.path` or `reviewer.agent.codexSdk.path` at the installed package directory. `reviewer.agent.model` takes a model name such as `"claude-haiku-5-5"` with these runtimes. Their reviews are recorded in the usage log read by `npx opencode-auto-approval-plugin stats`.

Note that auto mode may let the reviewer read files outside the project when it judges the read safe; use the default `opencode` runtime if that is not acceptable. See the README's "Agent runtimes" section for details.

* feat: run the agent reviewer on the Claude Agent SDK or the Codex SDK by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/54

## Contributors

* @dyoshikawa

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/compare/v0.7.0...v0.8.0

## What's Changed

### Features

- **Long context for Jev** — `reviewer.decision.longContext` (`typesafe` provider only, off by default) sends an operation larger than `maxStateTokens` whole with TypeSafe's long-context header (`TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context`, up to 262k tokens on Jev 1.13 and 1.14) instead of treating it as too large, up to `longContext.maxStateTokens` (default 240,000). Smaller operations are still sent without the header. Because TypeSafe documents long-context answers as less accurate, they need `allow` at `longContext.minAllowProbability` (default 0.8, or the regular threshold if higher, never below it), and the reason says `… with long context`. A regular request that Jev refuses as too long is asked once more with long context within the same timeout. See the README's "Long context (TypeSafe)" section. by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/48
- **Opt-in audit log** — `auditLog.enabled` with an absolute `auditLog.path` appends one JSONL record per review (time, backend, session, action, verdict, confidence, duration, error category) through a symlink-safe, mode-`0600` append. Command text is a separate opt-in (`auditLog.includeCommand`) with best-effort redaction. Works with every backend and both plugin API generations; POSIX only. by @InCerryGit in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/35
- **Opt-in conversation context** — `conversation.enabled` lets the reviewer see the session's recent user turns (at most 8 whole turns / 12,000 characters), so a short request such as "continue" can refer to an earlier instruction. Assistant turns are a further opt-in (`conversation.includeAssistant`) and are never treated as authorization. Every backend reviews the same state. by @InCerryGit in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/35

### Fixes

- The OpenCode 1.x handler now reads the modern `permission` / `patterns` permission fields, falling back to the legacy `type` / `pattern`; a malformed modern action is never approved. by @InCerryGit in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/34

### Security

- Set `auditLog` and `longContext` only in configuration you trust, like `baseURL` and `minAllowProbability`: a repository's `opencode.json` could point the audit log at a file it should not append to, or let larger operations be approved automatically.

### Dependencies

- Dependency and GitHub Actions updates (#42, #43, #45, #46).

## Contributors

- @dyoshikawa
- @InCerryGit

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/compare/v0.6.0...v0.7.0

## What's Changed

### Features

- **`chat` reviewer backend** — `reviewer.backend: "chat"` reviews each operation in one call to an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Workers AI, a local server) with the same prompt as the agent reviewer but no session and no tools. Configure `reviewer.chat` (`model`, plus `apiKey` and `baseURL` from the options, or `AUTO_APPROVAL_CHAT_API_KEY` / `AUTO_APPROVAL_CHAT_BASE_URL`). See the README's "Chat backend" section. by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/40
- **Oversize fallback for the decision backend** — an operation too large for the decision model is no longer sent as a truncated preview. Its size is estimated conservatively (Japanese counts as about one token a character) against `reviewer.decision.maxStateTokens` (28,000 for Jev, 20,000 for Clef), and Jev's `max_tokens_exceeded` is treated the same way. `reviewer.decision.onOversize` then escalates it (default) or hands it whole to the `"agent"` or `"chat"` reviewer, whose `allow` stands — useful where nobody can answer a prompt, such as OpenCode in a GitHub Actions workflow. by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/40
- **Clearer backend names** — the backends are now `agent` (was `opencode`), `chat` and `decision` (was `decision-model` / `jev`), with options under `reviewer.agent`, `reviewer.chat` and `reviewer.decision`. by @dyoshikawa in https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/pull/39

### Security

- LLM reviewers (agent and chat) now open every prompt with a random review check that the JSON answer must echo; a reply without it, or one whose reported prompt-token count is implausibly low, is treated as an operation the model did not read whole and escalates. The task and the answer format are restated after the operation data, the answer is the verdict object the reply ends with, and conflicting verdicts carrying the check are refused.
- Agent and chat prompts are bounded by `maxInputBytes` (UTF-8 bytes, default 200,000), so a session is not compacted and a local server's context is not silently overflowed.

### Deprecations

- `backend: "opencode"` with `reviewer.model`, `backend: "decision-model"` with `reviewer.decisionModel`, and `backend: "jev"` with `reviewer.jev` still work and mean the same thing. Setting a name next to its replacement fails at startup.

### Behavior changes

- The `agent` reviewer's answer must now echo the review check, and prompts over 200,000 bytes escalate unsent.
- Usage-log records may carry the new verdict `oversize`, and chat reviews are logged with `provider: "chat"`.

## Contributors

- @dyoshikawa

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/dyoshikawa/opencode-auto-approval-plugin/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0
